text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV).

The clinical presentation of brief, spontaneous vertigo episodes lasting less than a minute in an otherwise healthy patient, combined with normal cardiac and metabolic workup, is classic for BPPV. The negative neurological exam and imaging further support this peripheral etiology.
